words.row_comment: Algorithm enable flags word 7 (EEPROM 0x198; e2m 106B +10): the engine protection enables of channels 0-3 - coolant level 0x1-0x8 / coolant temperature 0x10-0x80 / intake manifold temperature 0x100-0x800 / oil pressure 0x1000-0x8000, four bits per channel: fueling limiting / rpm limiting / shutdown / restart (Calterm EPCV / EPCQ / EPIM / EPO2 + FLEN / RPEN / SOEN / RYEN; channel n = config record 0x807032 + 36 x n). The protection loops read them as table bit 0x70 + 4 x channel + k from word 0 (0x803c94): k 0 the fault derate fuel limit loop cm550_FUN_00019702, k 1 cm550_calculateFaultDerateEngineSpeedLimit, k 2 the shutdown loop processDiagnosticLimitStatus, k 2 and k 3 the restart checks cm550_diagnosticProtectionEvaluator / cm550_protectionState1DiagnosticValidator. One direct reader: cm550_FUN_00019702 tests 0x1000 at 0x1983e for the oil pressure start-up inhibit. No store in the dumped ROM. 0xffff in the EEPROM and RAM dumps (all four channels fully enabled). CM848 twin algorithm_enable_flags_7_cal (0x3fd5aa) has the same 16 e2m records but stays a plain word (nothing reads it there). (no row before; PR #53 round 92)
words.differences_from_cm848: No bit differs: CM848's word 7 (0x3fd5aa) has the same 16 e2m records at the same masks (Coolant_Level / Coolant_Temperature / IMT / Oil_Pressure x Fueling_Limiting / RPM_Limiting / Shutdown / Restart). But CM848 keeps it a plain word (its engine protection loops start at table bit 128 so nothing reads it) and has no algorithm_enable_flags_7_t, so there is no CM848 type to share: the type is CM550's own, with field names spelled from CM848's e2m record names. In CM550 the loops start at table bit 112 and channels 0-3 read all 16 bits.
words.code_tests: Direct: 0x1983e move.w (0x803ca2).l,d0 + andi.w #0x1000 + beq (cm550_FUN_00019702 @ 0x19702) = bit 12. Indexed from word 0 (movea.l #0x803c94,a0 then move.w (0,a0,dn.w*2): word = bit >> 4, mask = 1 << (bit & 15)): table bit 0x70 + 4 x channel + k, channels 0-3 = this word. k 0 cm550_FUN_00019702 (moveq #0x70 at 0x19718); k 1 cm550_calculateFaultDerateEngineSpeedLimit (moveq #0x71 at 0x18e22); k 2 processDiagnosticLimitStatus (moveq #0x72 at 0x1902a); k 2 and k 3 of the recorded shutdown channel in cm550_diagnosticProtectionEvaluator (addi.w #0x70 at 0x18b64, then +2 / +3) and cm550_protectionState1DiagnosticValidator (moveq #0x70 at 0x18cf8). What the bits do there: k 0 / k 1 - the loop computes the channel's fueling / rpm severity only while the bit or the channel's history-only bit (table bit 0x1a0 + channel = word 26) is set; k 2 - the channel's shutdown timers run only while set (clear zeroes them); k 3 - with k 2 set and the channel recorded as the shutdown channel, cm550_diagnosticProtectionEvaluator examines it before cranking once the shutdown count has reached its maximum (it skips channel 3) and cm550_protectionState1DiagnosticValidator updates its restart severity indexes. Channel identity from the extended RAM dump: each state record (0x80d0dc + 46 x channel) starts with the channel's input pointer - channel 0 0x8091e6 (the coolant level low switch input) / 1 0x80a336 (e2m ADCLTPFT filtered coolant temperature) / 2 0x80a26a (the intake manifold temperature pre-processed for engine protection) / 3 0x80a30a (ADOLPRFT filtered oil pressure). .cpp: 1 plain test, no value-flow form.
words.writes: none: the one absolute reference is the move.w read at 0x1983e, the indexed accesses are move.w reads, and nothing references the odd byte 0x803ca3. Only the generic EEPROM mirror writers can change it.

proposal.notes:
METHOD. Every absolute-long reference to 0x803ca2-0x803cb1 in J90350.00.rom.bin was found and decoded (scratch direct_tests.py): 29 move.w (abs).l,d0 reads, each followed by andi.w / andi.l with a single-bit mask and a branch, plus one address load (move.l #0x803cae,(0x80054c).l at 0x15dd2). No store, no btst, no byte access, no reference to an odd address and none to word 10 (0x803ca8). The indexed accesses use word 0 as their base; I hand-decoded two of them (0x19734-0x19756 and 0x208ce-0x208fc: moveq / addi the bit number, divide or mask by 16, lsl a 1, asr.l #4, move.w (0,a0,dn.w*2)) so table bit i = word i >> 4, mask 1 << (i & 15), and I read the loop constants in the machine code (moveq #0x70 / #0x71 / #0x72, addi.l #0xd0). llvm-objdump-18 and llvm-mc-18 drop many m68k opcodes, so the instruction addresses come from the byte scan and the behaviour from the committed .cpp. The nine protection channels are identified three ways that agree: the 106B records, the e2m names of each channel's own records (configs 0x807032 + 36n, states 0x80d0dc + 46n, severities 0x8057c0 + 30n) and the input pointer at the start of each state record in the extended RAM dump (read at file offset address - 0x809242, the dump being 0x80 short). Dump values: EEPROM 0x198-0x1a7 equals RAM 0x803ca2-0x803cb1 (w7 0xffff, w8 0, w9 0, w10 0, w11 0x000b, w12 0xbb87, w13 0, w14 0).

OLD NAMES AGAINST THE E2M WORD NUMBER. Only calibration_feature_enable_flags_word_9 (0x803cac) is misnumbered: (0x803cac - 0x803c94) / 2 = 12 and its records say WORD C. diagnostic_subsystem_enable_flags (word 11) is a wrong domain: the word enables the datalink protocols. switch_override_configuration (word 13) is right in substance. The e2m writes the word number in hex for word 12 (C) and in decimal for words 13 / 14 ('WORD 13 BIT 9', 'WORD 14 BIT 1'); both fit offset = 2 + 2 x n.

TYPES. Word 11 takes CM848's algorithm_enable_flags_11_t (the only shared type of the batch; check_shared_r92.py prints 'names equal' for it). Words 7 / 8 / 12 / 13 / 14 are cm550_ bitfields: each has direct single-bit tests and no store. Word 9 stays a plain word: nothing reads it by its own address (CM848's rule for its words 7 / 8 / 26), so its fields are for the row comment only.
- Word 7 is the one judgment call on the type: all 16 bits equal CM848's e2m records for its word 7, but CM848 has no algorithm_enable_flags_7_t (a plain word with no reader), so there is nothing to share and I used cm550_algorithm_enable_flags_7_t. If you would rather have one shared type, rename it algorithm_enable_flags_7_t and add the same rows to CM848 (its row can be retyped with no render change, since nothing reads it); the field names already follow CM848's e2m record names.

NAMING CHOICES TO REVIEW.
- Engine protection bits: <channel>_fueling_limiting_enable / _rpm_limiting_enable / _shutdown_enable / _restart_enable, after CM848's e2m record names (Coolant_Level_Fueling_Limiting_Enable ... Coolant_Level_Restart_Enable) and algorithm_enable_flags_2_t.engine_protection_restart_enable. The restart bit does not allow a restart: with the shutdown bit it lets the restart checks shut the engine down again ('PREVENTS RESTART AT POWERUP WHEN SHUTDN CNT > MAX SHUTDN CNT'). <channel>_restart_limitation_enable would say that more plainly (the e2m and CM848 both call the algorithm the restart limitation); I kept CM848's wording so the twins match. Channel names are the ones W4 used for word 26 (the same nine channels).
- Word 12 bits 8 / 9 take CM848's field names, which describe CM848's detectors; J90350.00 has no reader for them in the dump, only the same VSMVEN / VSSTEN records.
- Word 12 bit 5 keeps CM848's reverse_electronic_smart_power_enable (label Reverse_ESP_Enable); CM550's own text and code say ESP launch application (tau source state 1 of NORMAL / LAUNCH / STEEP).
